The test image shows a **cross-section of a corn ear (or stalk)** with:
- Tan/cream colored kernel segments arranged radially
- Pink to reddish-purple discoloration in the central pith area and between kernels
- Some white/tan powdery mold material in the center
- No olive-green or dark green mold

This points toward a pink/red rot. Top candidates: **Ear_rots_Gibberella** (pink-red mold from tip via silk), **Fusarium** (white to pink/salmon mold, starburst), or possibly stalk rot. Let me check references.

The test image shows a cross-sectional view with tan/cream kernel segments arranged radially, and pink to reddish-purple discoloration in the central cob/pith area with some white powdery material. Neither Fusarium (white-salmon mold on scattered kernels) nor Diplodia (white mold from base, tan-brown) match well. Let me check Gibberella ear rot and stalk rots more carefully.

Neither charcoal nor Diplodia stalk rot match the cross-sectional appearance with pink-reddish coloration. This strongly points to an ear rot. Let me confirm by checking the Gibberella and Ear_rots_Aspergillus references more carefully.

Neither Aspergillus (olive-green mold) nor Trichoderma (dark green mold) match. All other ear rot references show clearly different colors.

**Summary of evidence:**
- **Anatomy**: Cross-section of a corn ear viewed from the butt end — ~16-18 tan/cream kernel segments arranged radially around a central cob
- **Key diagnostic feature**: Pink to reddish-purple discoloration throughout the central cob tissue with some white powdery mold
- **Ruled out**: Fusarium (white-salmon scattered mold), Diplodia (white mold from base, tan-brown), Aspergillus (olive-green), Trichoderma (dark green), all stalk rots (shredded pith, dark/gray/black)
- **Matches**: Ear_rots_Gibberella — "pinkish-white to pink-red mold...pink to red kernel streaking" — the pink-red discoloration in the cob tissue of this cross-section is the hallmark of Gibberella ear rot caused by *Fusarium graminearum*
